name: Qwen3.8 27B official FP8 on two Intel Arc Pro B70 cards

library.summary: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 27B official block-FP8 weights on two Arc Pro B70 cards. The R156 profile (row-invariant W8A16 kernel plus a mixed-step GDN split) is clean-boot-qualified at 54.603 tok/s MTP1 (FP16 target verifier, draft-only INT4 head) and 33.314 tok/s MTP0. MTP0 output is byte-identical to a single request at every tested concurrency through 64 users; MTP1 through 16 users. Both are repeat-exact at every tested prompt length from 100 to 300 tokens. Independent host-installation replay passed on a second lab host; its slower CPU and fabric lower the single-user rate, see the guide's know-your-host section.
library.benchmark_status: Strict R156 promotion (2026-09-03, clean boot): two same-image MTP0 controls 33.326/33.302 tok/s matched 12/12; two MTP1 candidates 54.500/54.707 tok/s (center 54.603) matched 12/12 against each other and against the MTP0 oracle; canaries before and after every server; cache zero; repeat-exact at 100, 168, 200, 224, 250, and 300 prompt tokens on both profiles. Identity ladders (64 sequential oracles, then 1-64 concurrent users, 128 tokens each): MTP0 exact 64/64 through c64 (reproduced on three servers); MTP1 exact through c16, 31/32 at c32 and 56/64 at c64, so MTP1 aggregate rates are published only through c16. The R156 image is R139 plus a Python patch (vllm/_xpu_ops.py) that runs mixed prefill/decode GDN steps as pure calls; binaries are the R139 release. Independent host replay: recipe closure and all correctness gates pass on a Threadripper PRO/PCIe Gen4 host at 1.8x lower decode rate (host submission latency), recovered to 94% with XPU Graph on.

featured_metric.label: strict varied-prompt decode (R156 MTP1)
featured_metric.scope: Median of two clean-boot fresh-server class-balanced medians over the complete fixed 12-prompt/six-class natural-512 suite (48-78-token prompts), separate empty compile caches, 12/12 complete token arrays exact versus a same-image MTP0 oracle, canaries before and after, cache zero; repeat-exact at 100-300-token prompts; output-identical through 16 concurrent users (MTP0: through 64).

contributors.name: neural.download lab
contributors.contribution: B70/XPU integration, strict output validation, direct-I/O model verification, direct-P2P concurrency tuning, block-W8A16 dispatch, deterministic GDN state handling, explicit oneCCL completion ordering, exact packed MTP1 Gemma RMSNorm replay, dynamic-width GDN repair, active Mamba-state allocation, and the digest-pinned package.
contributors.validated_effect: The deterministic compiled TP2 work historically raised MTP0 from 18.910242 to 34.031596 tok/s, and block W8A16 separately raised matched target-only single/c128 shapes by 60.07%/29.30%. Clean-boot R119 qualified the draft-only INT4 R62 MTP1 profile at 54.424603 tok/s, 5.0504% above the prior qualified MTP1 profile, with both candidate and MTP0-oracle comparisons exact on 12/12 complete arrays in scope.

contributors.name: vLLM XPU kernel contributors
contributors.contribution: Split and corrected the native GDN speculative/non-speculative paths so continuous batching can mix MTP decode and newly arriving prefill rows.
contributors.validated_effect: The older kernel aborted the c16 mixed workload. With the pinned upstream correction integrated, c16 completed and the selected MTP1 profile reached 1091.642460 tok/s at c64 while passing 512/512 concurrent semantic checks.

project_patches.reason: The qualified R156 profile is the R62 image plus a Python mixed-step GDN split (vllm/_xpu_ops.py, VLLM_XPU_GDN_SPLIT_MIXED=1) and a rebuilt vllm-xpu-kernels extension whose oneDNN W8A16 GEMM uses a fixed-K row-invariant strategy selector (two oneDNN patches), so greedy output no longer depends on batch shape for batch sizes 1-512 and is repeat-exact at every prompt length. Everything else is the R62 chain: block-W8A16, deterministic GDN B/A and compiler-visible recurrent state, explicit oneCCL Work.wait, packed Gemma RMSNorm serial replay, the content-verified R50 GDN build, the deterministic vLLM compilation contract with XPU Graph disabled, and draft-only INT4 vocabulary projection with an FP16 target verifier. The compiled extension is published as a release binary with whole-file and section digests, and can be rebuilt from the pinned sources with host oneAPI 2026.1. Dynamic MTP additionally requires the active-width GDN and active-lookahead Mamba allocation patches and remains research-only.

performance_profiles.label: R156 FP8 TP2 + MTP1 aggregate decode, output-identical through c16
performance_profiles.scope: Measured vLLM HTTP completions on two B70s with the R156 image (MTP1, FP16 verifier, draft-only INT4 head), FP16 activations/KV, 64 service slots, 256-token total request capacity, max_num_batched_tokens=512, cache disabled, 128 returned raw token IDs per response on the 64-prompt small-context suite. Every point shown is output-identity-qualified: each concurrent output equals its own sequential oracle byte for byte (harness --require-output-identity). c32 and c64 were measured but are withheld: 1/32 and 8/64 near-tie prompts took a different valid branch. One server, one pass per point; not a promoted concurrency speed record.

performance_profiles.label: Official FP8 TP2 HTTP median TTFT under concurrency
performance_profiles.scope: Measured on the previous R50/R62 image (natural oneDNN W8A16 kernel), not yet re-measured on R139. Median request TTFT from the same two fresh-server, output-audited direct-P2P attempts. The service has 64 active slots, so c1-c64 are unqueued. Each point is the median of the two per-attempt p50 values; worst latency range across every reported p50/p95 metric was 4.404%. No point is interpolated or extrapolated.
